title: Employers' rights and responsibilities
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:12Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: No bank point covers both the employer's legal duties (correct pay, safety, fair treatment) and the employer's reasonable expectations of staff (working properly, following reasonable instructions) for this NSW course, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Employers' rights and responsibilities
card: An employer must pay at least the correct wages and entitlements, such as the pay rate set by the award or agreement that covers the job.
An employer must also provide a safe workplace. This means finding hazards, fixing them and giving staff training and equipment.
An employer must treat staff fairly. That includes not discriminating against them or harassing them.
An employer can expect staff to turn up and work properly. They can also expect staff to follow reasonable instructions about the job.
draft.remember: Employers owe pay, safety and fair treatment, and can expect proper work and reasonable instructions.

a.q: Tariq owns a bakery in Newcastle. Which of these is his responsibility as an employer?
opts: Fixing a faulty oven that could burn staff
Deciding which shifts his staff enjoy most
Making sure staff arrive on time each day
Telling staff how to wear their hair at home
a.why: An employer must provide a safe workplace, and a faulty oven is a hazard to fix. Expecting staff to arrive on time is a right of the employer, not a responsibility owed to staff.
a.clue: Think about what the employer owes staff, not what the employer can expect from them.

b.q: Lena manages a gym in Wollongong. She tells a trainer to wipe down equipment after each class. The trainer refuses and says it is not in the job. Which statement is correct?
opts: Lena is using her right to give a reasonable instruction
Lena is breaking her duty to keep staff safe
Lena must pay extra before she can give any instruction
Lena can only ask for tasks written in the job title
b.why: Wiping equipment is a reasonable instruction linked to the job, and employers can expect staff to follow such instructions. The tempting option about safety is wrong because the task is not a hazard.
b.clue: Is the task reasonable and linked to the work?

a.best: Fixing a faulty oven that could burn staff

b.best: Lena is using her right to give a reasonable instruction
